status: All four Linux/macOS jobs, both repaired Windows jobs and both actual WASI jobs pass; runtime/compiler/library sources are identical between focused heads
workload: Real local TCP traffic, original function scopes and captured listeners, rebinding, timeout, cancellation, multiple pending accepts, 301 logical owners, allocation failures during listener/connection/optional-value construction, actual library load/unload and mutual TLS. Windows live-listener bind behavior and TLS socket-error capture match the interpreter.
validation: Raw and optimized interpreter outputs match O1/O2 tracing stress/reuse and checked ARC. Initialized scheduler probes return charged storage to their starting budget without collections. An ARC executable probe rejects any unused finalizer-table lookup. Library tests retain three TCP descriptors or one UDP descriptor across three load/unload cycles; the host socket remains live. Omitted-cleanup controls fail. Mutual TLS compares successful and rejected client certificates with the interpreter, checks the actual ARC executable for absence of tracing functions, and retains that binary. Deterministic TLS read/write/handshake controls distinguish a socket reset from clean shutdown and readiness waits; ignoring socket errors must fail. POSIX TLS teardown and session-transfer controls run on Linux/macOS.
limits: No throughput or C/Rust performance claim. Returning to the initialized managed-storage budget does not mean zero process memory: allocator reservations, scheduler state, OS sockets and OpenSSL have costs. Shared socket values retain a logical count. Scope preservation for opaque closures can inhibit optimization. The retained lifetime probes include storage-check instrumentation, not a timing harness. Socket-library and POSIX teardown outcomes are retained in job logs, not separate archived library binaries. WASI tests cover shared-runtime regressions, not networking support. General service/callback lifetime and whole-language collector removal remain unfinished. Full combined production acceptance is separate.
layout: Common headers store a descriptor, kind and aligned 64-bit owner count. UDP/plain-TCP programs preserve the previous size; TCP handles in TLS-enabled programs add one session pointer within the same allocation. Native static assertions check each host. ARM64 executable inspection is recorded separately after downloading the exact binaries.
windowsHarnessFix: The Windows-only run adds .exe to the inspected TLS executable path and selects the Windows API version before injected OpenSSL headers. Linux/macOS and WASI keep their exact-runtime evidence; final full acceptance is required on the combined head.
